OpenWhispr

The open-source and free alternative to WisprFlow and Granola.
Privacy-first voice-to-text dictation with AI agents, meeting transcription, and notes. Cross-platform for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Website · Docs · Download · API · Changelog

--- OpenWhispr turns your voice into text, notes, and actions from your desktop. Press a hotkey, speak, and your words appear at your cursor. Choose between fully private offline transcription with local speech-to-text models like Orukeet, Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet, and Cohere Transcribe — where your audio never leaves your device — or cloud processing for speed. No data collection, no telemetry, fully open source. ## Download | Platform | Download | | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | [`.dmg`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | macOS (Intel) \* | [`.dmg`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | Windows | [`.exe`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | Linux | [`.AppImage`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.deb`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.rpm`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.tar.gz`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | \* On Intel Macs, live speaker identification and voice fingerprinting are unavailable: they depend on ONNX Runtime, which [stopped shipping macOS x86_64 binaries in 1.24](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/tag/v1.24.1). Meetings still record and transcribe normally, and notes search falls back to keyword matching instead of semantic search. On macOS or x86_64 Linux, you can also install the community-maintained [Homebrew cask](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/openwhispr): ```bash brew install --cask openwhispr ``` ## Features - **Voice dictation** — global hotkey to dictate into any app with automatic pasting - **Dictation translation** — dedicated hotkey to dictate in one language and paste the text in another - **AI agent** — talk to GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, Groq, Tinfoil, OpenRouter, or local models with a named voice assistant - **Voice Assistant hotkey** — dedicated hotkey that sends what you say straight to your AI assistant as a command, no wake word needed and no cleanup pass; highlighted text is edited in place. With auto-paste enabled, answers paste at a focused text cursor or stream into a floating panel and copy to the clipboard when no writable cursor is available. You can also opt in to sending a screenshot of your current screen as context - **Meeting transcription** — auto-detect Zoom, Teams, and FaceTime calls with live speaker diarization, voice fingerprinting, and Google, Microsoft, or Apple Calendar integration - **Local speaker diarization** — on-device speaker labelling with voice fingerprint recognition across meetings, no cloud required - **Notes** — create, organize, and search notes with folders, semantic search, cloud sync, and AI actions - **Team spaces & sharing** — free for signed-in users; share notes on the web with link, domain, or invite-only visibility, and collaborate in team spaces with roles, invitations, and server-enforced membership - **Audio import** — transcribe existing audio and video: drag in files, batch-upload, or paste a YouTube/audio URL, with optional speaker detection - **Local or cloud — your choice** — all core features (transcription, AI reasoning, speaker diarization, semantic search) work with local models or cloud providers — including GPU-accelerated local Whisper on Metal, CUDA, and Vulkan (AMD/Intel) - **Enterprise controls** — enforce organization policy, company SSO and SCIM, and centrally managed Amazon Bedrock or Azure OpenAI access without distributing cloud keys - **Public API & MCP** — manage notes and transcriptions programmatically or connect your AI assistant via the [MCP server](https://docs.openwhispr.com/integrations/mcp) ## Free vs. paid OpenWhispr is MIT-licensed. Everything that runs on your device is free, with no account and no word limit: | Free from OpenWhispr (on-device or your own keys) | Free OpenWhispr Cloud | Paid Cloud plans | | --- | --- | --- | | Local transcription (Whisper, Parakeet, Cohere, Orukeet) | 2,000 hosted words/week | Unlimited cloud transcription | | Local AI models and the local AI agent | 5 hours of meeting recordings/month | 20 hours/month (Pro) or unlimited (Business) meeting recordings | | Local speaker diarization | Teamspaces for signed-in users | Sync across devices | | Local notes, folders, and semantic search\* | | Public note links | | Custom dictionary and 100+ languages | | Personal API access and MCP integration | | Cloud transcription with your own API keys (provider charges and limits apply) | | Mobile app, workspace roles, and SSO | The free Cloud allowance is 2,000 words/week and 5 hours of meeting recordings/month; the remaining Cloud features in the third column require a paid plan. Teamspaces are free for signed-in users; creating a team inside a workspace requires the Business plan. See **Settings → Plans** in the app for current pricing. \* On Intel Macs, notes search falls back to keyword matching instead of semantic search. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr.git cd openwhispr npm install npm run dev ``` Requires Node.js 24+. See the [full documentation](https://docs.openwhispr.com/quickstart) for setup guides, platform-specific instructions, and build details. The list of models the desktop app offers lives in [`model-registry`](model-registry/); see its [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](model-registry/CONTRIBUTING.md) to add or correct a model. The commands above run the desktop application, which remains at the repository root. The Expo mobile application lives in [`openwhispr-mobile`](openwhispr-mobile/) with its own dependencies, lockfile, build configuration, and release process. See the [mobile README](openwhispr-mobile/README.md) for its setup instructions. ## Documentation Visit **[docs.openwhispr.com](https://docs.openwhispr.com)** for: - [Getting started](https://docs.openwhispr.com/quickstart) - [Platform guides](https://docs.openwhispr.com/platform/macos) (macOS, Windows, Linux) - [API reference](https://docs.openwhispr.com/api/overview) - [MCP server setup](https://docs.openwhispr.com/integrations/mcp) - [Troubleshooting](https://docs.openwhispr.com/troubleshooting) Repo examples: - [Custom ASR shim](examples/custom-asr-shim/) for Self-Hosted transcription against non-OpenAI-compatible ASR APIs ## Tech stack React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Electron 41, better-sqlite3, whisper.cpp, sherpa-onnx, shadcn/ui ## Star History ## Sponsors

Neon is the serverless Postgres platform powering OpenWhispr Cloud.

## Contributing We welcome contributions. Fork the repo, create a feature branch, and open a pull request. See the [contributing guide](https://docs.openwhispr.com/contributing) for development setup and guidelines. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) — free for personal and commercial use. ## Acknowledgments - **[OpenAI Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper)** — speech recognition model powering local and cloud transcription - **[whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp)** — high-performance C++ implementation for local processing - **[NVIDIA Parakeet](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3)** — fast multilingual ASR model - **[sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx)** — cross-platform ONNX runtime for Parakeet inference - **[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/)** — model hub hosting Whisper, Parakeet, and embedding model weights - **[llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp)** — local LLM inference for AI text processing - **[Electron](https://www.electronjs.org/)** — cross-platform desktop framework - **[React](https://react.dev/)** — UI component library - **[shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/)** — accessible components built on Radix primitives - **[Neon](https://console.neon.tech/app/?promo=openwhispr)** — serverless Postgres powering OpenWhispr Cloud

Website · Docs · Download · API · Changelog

OpenWhispr turns your voice into text, notes, and actions from your desktop. Press a hotkey, speak, and your words appear at your cursor. Choose between fully private offline transcription with local speech-to-text models like Orukeet, Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet, and Cohere Transcribe — where your audio never leaves your device — or cloud processing for speed. No data collection, no telemetry, fully open source.

Download

Platform Download
macOS (Apple Silicon) .dmg
macOS (Intel) * .dmg

* On Intel Macs, live speaker identification and voice fingerprinting are unavailable: they depend on ONNX Runtime, which stopped shipping macOS x86_64 binaries in 1.24. Meetings still record and transcribe normally, and notes search falls back to keyword matching instead of semantic search.

On macOS or x86_64 Linux, you can also install the community-maintained Homebrew cask:

brew install --cask openwhispr

Features

  • Voice dictation — global hotkey to dictate into any app with automatic pasting
  • Dictation translation — dedicated hotkey to dictate in one language and paste the text in another
  • AI agent — talk to GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, Groq, Tinfoil, OpenRouter, or local models with a named voice assistant
  • Voice Assistant hotkey — dedicated hotkey that sends what you say straight to your AI assistant as a command, no wake word needed and no cleanup pass; highlighted text is edited in place. With auto-paste enabled, answers paste at a focused text cursor or stream into a floating panel and copy to the clipboard when no writable cursor is available. You can also opt in to sending a screenshot of your current screen as context
  • Meeting transcription — auto-detect Zoom, Teams, and FaceTime calls with live speaker diarization, voice fingerprinting, and Google, Microsoft, or Apple Calendar integration
  • Local speaker diarization — on-device speaker labelling with voice fingerprint recognition across meetings, no cloud required
  • Notes — create, organize, and search notes with folders, semantic search, cloud sync, and AI actions
  • Team spaces & sharing — free for signed-in users; share notes on the web with link, domain, or invite-only visibility, and collaborate in team spaces with roles, invitations, and server-enforced membership
  • Audio import — transcribe existing audio and video: drag in files, batch-upload, or paste a YouTube/audio URL, with optional speaker detection
  • Local or cloud — your choice — all core features (transcription, AI reasoning, speaker diarization, semantic search) work with local models or cloud providers — including GPU-accelerated local Whisper on Metal, CUDA, and Vulkan (AMD/Intel)
  • Enterprise controls — enforce organization policy, company SSO and SCIM, and centrally managed Amazon Bedrock or Azure OpenAI access without distributing cloud keys
  • Public API & MCP — manage notes and transcriptions programmatically or connect your AI assistant via the MCP server

Free vs. paid

OpenWhispr is MIT-licensed. Everything that runs on your device is free, with no account and no word limit:

Free from OpenWhispr (on-device or your own keys) Free OpenWhispr Cloud Paid Cloud plans
Local transcription (Whisper, Parakeet, Cohere, Orukeet) 2,000 hosted words/week Unlimited cloud transcription
Local AI models and the local AI agent 5 hours of meeting recordings/month 20 hours/month (Pro) or unlimited (Business) meeting recordings
Local speaker diarization Teamspaces for signed-in users Sync across devices
Local notes, folders, and semantic search* Public note links
Custom dictionary and 100+ languages Personal API access and MCP integration
Cloud transcription with your own API keys (provider charges and limits apply) Mobile app, workspace roles, and SSO

The free Cloud allowance is 2,000 words/week and 5 hours of meeting recordings/month; the remaining Cloud features in the third column require a paid plan. Teamspaces are free for signed-in users; creating a team inside a workspace requires the Business plan. See Settings → Plans in the app for current pricing.

* On Intel Macs, notes search falls back to keyword matching instead of semantic search.

Quick start

git clone https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr.git
cd openwhispr
npm install
npm run dev

Requires Node.js 24+. See the full documentation for setup guides, platform-specific instructions, and build details.

The list of models the desktop app offers lives in model-registry; see its CONTRIBUTING.md to add or correct a model.

The commands above run the desktop application, which remains at the repository root. The Expo mobile application lives in openwhispr-mobile with its own dependencies, lockfile, build configuration, and release process. See the mobile README for its setup instructions.

# OpenWhispr 1.12.0

A new assistant window you can talk to from any app, Private notes and Teams for workspaces, and one-screen local setup.

## 🌟 Highlights

- **🎙️ A new assistant window** — Press the assistant hotkey in any app and speak or type. It answers in its own window, edits the text you selected, or types the answer into the field you're in. It asks you questions mid-task, drafts emails and Slack replies for you to edit and send, and keeps your chat when you minimize it.
- **🔒 Private notes** — Every workspace gets a Private section for your own notes, and it follows you across devices.
- **👥 Teams, Teamspaces and Guests** — A People page with bulk invites and removals, plus an overview of every teamspace.
- **🧭 One-screen local setup** — Recommended models for your computer, downloaded for you.
- **📡 Signed model registry** — New and retired models arrive between releases. Turn it off in Settings → Privacy.
- **💬 Background chats** — Leave a chat mid-answer and it keeps going, and several can answer at once.
- **🏢 Organization controls** — Managed device policy, update policy and local model allow lists.

- The assistant replies i

# OpenWhispr 1.11.0

Teams can now share a dictionary, the assistant can follow skills you keep for recurring work, and a bunch of new models.

## 🌟 Highlights

- **📚 Shared team dictionary** — Business and Enterprise members get their team's words in dictation and meeting notes. Your own words still come first.
- **🧩 Skills** — Save instructions for recurring work in Integrations → Skills. The assistant picks a fitting skill on its own.
- **🤖 New models** — GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude 5.5 on Bedrock, Gemma 4, Qwen3.8 and more. Older models keep working if you already use them.
- **🏢 Workspace switcher** — Switch workspaces and invite people from the sidebar. Your account now lives under your avatar in the top bar.
- **⚡ Whisper GPU fallback** — Whisper checks that CUDA or Vulkan actually started and falls back to CPU if not.


## 🛠 Fixes

- The app now starts after a second account signs in on the same device.
- On macOS, slow apps get your transcript, not your old clipboard. On Windows, AltGr no longer triggers Ctrl+Alt hotkeys.
- Meeting transcripts survive recording again, uploaded audio lands in the Transcript tab, and meeting prompts show up w

# OpenWhispr 1.10.4

Tone & Style writes your dictation, and the assistant's drafts, in the tone you pick for each kind of app. The AI Summary is more detailed by default, notes can link to a calendar event, and you can set a reasoning effort per model scope.

## 🌟 Highlights

- **🎨 Tone & Style** — Pick a tone for personal messages, work chats, email and everything else, and cleanup writes in it for the app you're in. Off by default; turn it on in Settings → Tone & Style.
- **📝 Detailed AI Summary** — Generate AI Summary now writes the same notes as the Detailed Notes template.
- **📅 Calendar events on notes** — Link any note to its meeting to pull in the guests and join link.
- **🧠 Reasoning effort** — Choose how hard reasoning models think, per scope.
- **❓ Ask about OpenWhispr** — The chat answers questions about the app from the docs and your settings.

## ✨ Also new

"This is me" in the speaker picker, searchable overflow for long sidebar folders, onboarding key checks as you type, Claude 5.5 models, and Qwen3.8 27B on Groq.

Prebuilt Linux text monitor binary for auto-learn correction monitoring.

This binary uses AT-SPI2 to detect text field changes after paste.

# OpenWhispr 1.10.3

The assistant can now act in other apps: it drafts and sends email, posts to Slack, and works with Linear and GitHub issues, always behind a card you approve. Notes get templates for the AI Summary, actions that answer in a docked chat, and real tables. OpenWhispr also uses far less memory when idle, shows a plain-language error when your API key or provider fails, and fixes a long list of bugs on Linux, Windows and macOS.

## 🌟 Highlights

- **🔌 Connectors** — The assistant can draft and send email (Gmail), post to Slack, and work with Linear and GitHub issues. Nothing goes out until you press **Send** on a card showing exactly what will be sent. Paid plans; connect in Settings → Integrations. (#2331, #2369, #2385, #2401, #2402)
- **📝 Note templates and actions** — Templates shape the AI Summary, and actions like Follow-up email answer in a chat docked beside the note instead of overwriting your summary. (#2397, #2557, #2578, #2598)

aiSummary.oneLiner: Cross-platform voice-to-text dictation application utilizing local Nvidia Parakeet and Whisper models.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OpenWhispr provides a privacy-focused dictation service that processes speech locally using powerful models like Nvidia Parakeet and Whisper. It offers a cross-platform desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux, ensuring users can dictate text directly into their system. It also supports BYOK for cloud model integration if users prefer remote processing. By running models entirely on-device, it guarantees that sensitive voice data never leaves the user's hardware.
keyFeatures: Local processing: Runs Nvidia Parakeet and Whisper models directly on the host machine for complete privacy.
Cross-platform support: Provides native applications for macOS, Windows, and Linux operating systems.
Cloud model integration: Allows users to bring their own API keys to utilize cloud-based dictation services.
Privacy-first design: Ensures no voice data is transmitted externally when using local models.
System-wide dictation: Integrates seamlessly to input text into any active application or field.

useCases.title: Secure dictation
useCases.description: Transcribe sensitive medical or legal notes without transmitting audio to third-party servers.

useCases.title: Offline transcription
useCases.description: Dictate text while traveling or working in environments without internet access.

useCases.title: Developer accessibility
useCases.description: Write code and documentation hands-free using high-accuracy voice recognition.

useCases.title: Content creation
useCases.description: Draft long-form articles or books quickly by speaking rather than typing.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Professionals handling sensitive information, developers, and writers who require accurate, privacy-respecting voice-to-text capabilities. It is ideal for users who prefer local model execution over cloud-based alternatives.
